records.label: Proband (young consanguineous girl)
records.segregation: Inherited from each healthy heterozygous parent
quotes: Here, we study a case of recessive EDS in a young consanguineous girl of healthy parents. She fulfilled the vascular EDS criteria for laboratory testing.

Total sequencing of COL3A1 cDNA identified a homozygous nucleotide duplication (c.479dupT) resulting in a premature termination codon (p.Lys161GlnfsX45). Studies in genomic DNA showed that this mutation was inherited from each parent.

records.label: III-2 (proband)

phenotypes.text: cystic medial necrosis of aortic wall
pale translucent skin with visible subcutaneous vessels
characteristic facial features (small lower jaw, prominent eyes, pinched nose, thin upper lip)

records.segregation: Nonsense variant from father, missense from mother (in trans); unaffected brother had neither
quotes: The proband was born with right-sided clubfoot and developed unilateral hydrocele of the testis

Autopsy revealed three dissections: a transverse dissection including nearly the whole circumference of the thoracic aorta at the level of ligamentum arteriosus, and separate dissections of the right renal artery and the left femoral artery.

The mother (II-6) was heterozygous for the COL3A1 c.3851G>A, p.(Gly1284Glu) sequence variant, and the father (II-5) was heterozygous for the COL3A1 c.1786C>T, p.(Arg596*) sequence variant, which confirmed that the variants were in trans.

records.label: III-3

phenotypes.text: stenosis of right external iliac artery
translucent skin with visible subcutaneous vessels
rupture of medial meniscus and anterior cruciate ligament
intermittent abdominal pain, diarrhea, and blood in stool
increased wall thickness of transverse colon

records.segregation: Nonsense variant from father, missense from mother (in trans)
quotes: She had cerebral cortical dysplasia with thickened frontoparietal cortices bilaterally, small gyri and findings consistent with pachy micropolygyria (Figures 1c and d). She had normal cognitive functioning, a recent neurological examination was normal and she had not experienced epileptic seizures.

MR arteriography (Figure 1a) and CT angiography revealed a stenotic process in her right internal carotid (ICA) and ultrasonography of neck vessels proved to represent a dissection (data not shown). The left ICA was ectatic.

The siblings III-2 and III-3 both manifested pale, translucent skin with visible subcutaneous vessels and facial features characteristic of EDS type IV with a small lower jaw, prominent eyes, pinched nose, and thin upper lip.

records.label: Family with two affected siblings
quotes: Exome analysis was performed in a family consisting of two affected and two non-affected siblings.

Exome analysis revealed a novel homozygous variant c.145C>G (p.Pro49Ala) in exon 2 of COL3A1. Brain MRI in the affected siblings as well as in the two previously reported individuals with bi-allelic COL3A1 mutations showed a brain phenotype similar to that associated with mutations in GPR56.

records.label: Two previously reported individuals with bi-allelic COL3A1 mutations
quotes: Brain imaging studies of this family and of two previously reported individuals with bi-allelic mutations in COL3A1 were reviewed.
Homozygous or compound heterozygous mutations in COL3A1 are associated with cobblestone-like malformation in all three families reported to date.

records.label: 3-year-old female

phenotypes.text: aneurysmal brain hemorrhage at age 2 years
bilateral frontoparietal polymicrogyria of the cobblestone variant

quotes: In a 3-year-old female with developmental delay the nonsense variant c.1282C>T, p.(Arg428*) was detected in combination the c.2057delC, p.(Pro686Leufs*105) frame shift variant. Both compound heterozygous variants were novel.
This patient was born with bilateral clubfoot, joint laxity, and dysmorphic facial features. At the age of 2 years she developed an aneurysmal brain hemorrhage.
Cerebral MRI showed a peculiar pattern of profound cerebral abnormalities including bilateral frontoparietal polymicrogyria of the cobblestone variant.

records.label: Second family, two affected siblings
quotes: In the second family, the two affected siblings were homozygous for the missense variant c.145C<G, p.(Pro49Ala) of COL3A1 and showed cobblestone-like cortical malformation, cerebellar cysts, and white matter abnormalities, developmental delay, and seizures.

notes.statement: Horn et al. (2017) noted that, including 3 previously reported families, all families with biallelic COL3A1 variants had specific structural brain anomalies, with a severe Ehlers-Danlos syndrome phenotype in some. Bilateral frontoparietal polymicrogyria of the cobblestone variant, cerebellar microcysts, and white matter abnormalities characterized the brain phenotype, resembling that of individuals with recessive GPR56 mutations.
quotes: To date, three further families have been reported with biallelic variants of this gene and specific structural brain anomalies in all, and a severe Ehlers-Danlos syndrome phenotype in some.

Bilateral frontoparietal polymicrogyria of the cobblestone variant, cerebellar microcysts, and abnormalities of the white matter characterize this brain phenotype and resemble neurological manifestations in individuals with autosomal recessive mutations in GPR56, which serves as a ligand of COL3A1.

notes.statement: Horn et al. (2017) concluded that, in concordance with findings in knockout mice, collagen III plays a role in the regulation of cortical development in addition to its function in connective tissue formation.
quotes: In concordance with the findings in knock out mice, the collagen III protein plays a role in the regulation of cortical development in addition to its well-known function in connective tissue formation.

notes.statement: Vandervore et al. (2017) noted that the phenotype varied across patients with bi-allelic COL3A1 mutations. They suggested that genetic changes in different domains of type III procollagen can lead to different outcomes.
quotes: The variability of the phenotype across patients suggests that genetic alterations in distinct domains of type III procollagen can lead to different outcomes.

notes.statement: Vandervore et al. (2017) noted that type III procollagen is the ligand of GPR56 and that bi-allelic GPR56 mutations cause a similar cobblestone-like malformation. They concluded that cobblestone-like malformation in patients with bi-allelic COL3A1 mutations highlights the critical role of the type III collagen-GPR56 axis and the pial membrane in brain development and cortical lamination.
quotes: Type III procollagen, the chains of which are encoded by COL3A1, is the ligand of the G protein-coupled receptor 56 (GPR56), also known as adhesion G protein-coupled receptor G1.

The presence of cobblestone-like malformation in patients with bi-allelic COL3A1 mutations emphasises the critical role of the type III collagen-GPR56 axis and the pial membrane in the regulation of brain development and cortical lamination.

notes.statement: Jørgensen et al. (2015) found that cultured dermal fibroblasts from the compound heterozygous patient produced a reduced amount of type III procollagen, all chains of which had abnormal electrophoretic mobility consistent with overmodification. Fibroblasts from the mother, heterozygous for the missense variant, produced mostly normal and a small amount of abnormal type III procollagen, and those from the father, heterozygous for the nonsense variant, produced a reduced amount of apparently normal type III procollagen.
quotes: Cultured dermal fibroblasts from III-3 produced a reduced amount of type III procollagen, the chains of which all had an abnormal electrophoretic mobility (Figure 2b).

Dermal fibroblasts from II-6, heterozygous for the missense mutation, produced mostly normal and a small amount of abnormal type III procollagen in which there was subtle overmodification of the chains. Dermal fibroblasts from II-5 heterozygous for the nonsense mutation produced a reduced amount of apparently normal type III procollagen.

notes.statement: Jørgensen et al. (2015) noted that heterozygous carriers in the family showed marked clinical variability: the father, carrying the nonsense variant, had no abnormal findings at age 63, and paternal relatives with the variant had no vEDS features, whereas the mother, carrying the missense variant, had thin skin, visible vessels, and reduced ascending aortic elasticity but not a complete vascular EDS picture by age 60.
quotes: the father (c.1786C>T, p.(Arg596*)) did not have abnormal clinical findings at age 63 and the mother (c.3851G>A, p.(Gly1284Glu)) did not express a complete picture of vascular-type EDS by age 60.
None of the individuals with the variant in the father's family had complications or clinical features consistent with the diagnosis of vEDS.

notes.statement: Jørgensen et al. (2015) suggested that the interaction of type III collagen with GPR56, mutations in which cause recessive bilateral frontoparietal polymicrogyria, defines a pathway in frontal brain formation, and that a recessive syndromic form of vascular EDS includes tissue fragility and cerebrocortical anomalies; they could not exclude a coincidental finding or variants in a second gene.
quotes: Our clinical findings and those described by Plancke et al suggest that the interaction of GPR56 and type III (pro)collagen identifies two parts of a pathway involved in frontotemporal brain formation.
suggests that a novel syndromic form of recessively inherited vascular Ehlers–Danlos includes both tissue fragility and cerebrocortical anomalies.
We cannot be sure if the vEDS phenotype with biallelic COL3A1 sequence variants and cerebrocortical findings in two separate patients are coincidental findings

notes.statement: Jørgensen et al. (2015) predicted that the G1284E substitution alters a highly conserved residue adjacent to a cysteine involved in interchain disulfide bonding in the C-propeptide, within a calcium-binding region, slowing trimer assembly.
quotes: Substitution of glycine by glutamic acid at position 1284 of the proα1(III) chain (p.Gly1284Glu) predicts the change of a highly conserved amino acid that is adjacent to the one of two cysteine residues involved in interchain, intramolecular disulfide bond formation

notes.statement: Jeong et al. (2012) found that Col3a1-null mice had a cobblestone-like cortical malformation. Its features were pial basement membrane breakdown, neuronal overmigration, abnormal attachment of radial glial endfeet, and marginal zone heterotopias. Ectopias were seen in 23 of 28 null embryos and in none of the wildtype or heterozygous embryos.
quotes: We have shown that homozygous deletion of Col3a1 causes cobblestone-like cortical malformation characterized by pial BM breakdown, neuronal overmigration, radial glial detachment, and formation of marginal zone heterotopias.

notes.statement: Jeong et al. (2012) found that the pial basement membrane formed normally in Col3a1-null mice at embryonic day (E) 10.5. Regional breakdown of the membrane, with neurons migrating past it at the same time, appeared in about half of E11.5 embryos and in all embryos older than E12.5. Cortical neurons from both deep and superficial layers, Cajal-Retzius cells, and interneurons were found in the ectopias.
quotes: Interestingly, in spite of the absence of collagen III, the pial BM was initially properly formed at E10.5 in the mutant mice (Figure 3J). Regional breakdown of the pial BM with concurrent neuronal overmigration was observed in about half of the E11.5 and all embryos older than E12.5 in the Col3a1 −/− brains analyzed

Neurons positive for Cux1, Tbr1 and CTIP2 were detected in the ectopias, suggesting that the ectopic cells in the Col3a1 −/− cortex were neurons from both deep and superficial cortical layers, mirroring our observations of Gpr56 null mutant mice

notes.statement: Jeong et al. (2012) found no obvious defects in meningeal fibroblasts from Col3a1-null mice. Expression and glycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan were also unchanged. The authors suggested that collagen III, a ligand of GPR56, regulates cortical development independently of the dystroglycan pathway.
quotes: We failed to detect any change in the level of α-dystroglycan in the brains of Col3a1 −/− mice, arguing that the function of collagen III does not directly affect the expression and glycosylation of dystroglycan (Figure 7).

However, we detected no obvious defects in the MFs of the Col3a1 −/− mice, suggesting that the cortical dyslamination seen in Col3a1 −/− mice is not the direct result of cellular defects of MFs, but rather the absence of collagen III, the ligand of GPR56.

notes.statement: Jeong et al. (2012) suggested that mutations in both alleles of COL3A1 may be associated with a lethal form of cobblestone lissencephaly similar to Walker-Warburg syndrome. They also suggested that connective tissue diseases and brain malformations may share a common pathologic pathway.
quotes: It is possible that mutations in both alleles of COL3A1 associate with a lethal form of cobblestone lissencephaly similar to WWS.
our study indicates a possible common pathological pathway linking connective tissue diseases and brain malformations

notes.statement: Plancke et al. (2009) found by RT-PCR, quantitative PCR, immunohistochemistry, and Western blot that the homozygous c.479dupT COL3A1 mutation caused strong mRNA decay and absence of type III collagen in the proband.
quotes: The expression analysis (RT-PCR, quantitative-PCR, immunohistochemistry, WB) showed strong mRNA decay and an absence of type III collagen in the proband.

notes.statement: Plancke et al. (2009) noted that the expected COL3A1 haploinsufficiency in the healthy heterozygous relatives did not cause vascular EDS. They suggested a stochastic effect of COL3A1 haploinsufficiency, possibly explained by the relation between nonsense-mediated decay efficiency and dominant-negative effect depending on mutation position and/or modifying factors.
quotes: The expected COL3A1 haploinsufficiency in her healthy ascendants did not lead to the manifestations of vascular EDS.

This case provides evidence of a stochastic effect of COL3A1 haploinsufficiency in humans, which could be explained by the relation between nonsense-mediated mRNA decay efficiency and the resulting dominant-negative effect depending on the position of the mutation and/or modifying factors.

notes.statement: Schwarze et al. (2001) found that the mRNAs from three COL3A1 frameshift alleles were transcribed efficiently but degraded rapidly, presumably by nonsense-mediated decay. In contrast, the mRNA from the final-exon nonsense mutation was stable, but the truncated protein it encoded was not incorporated into mature type III procollagen molecules.
quotes: The mRNA from each mutant allele was transcribed efficiently but rapidly degraded, presumably by the mechanisms of nonsense-mediated decay.
In this last instance, the mRNA was stable but led to synthesis of a truncated protein that was not incorporated into mature type III procollagen molecules.

notes.statement: Schwarze et al. (2001) concluded that, unlike null mutations in COL1A1 and COL2A1, null mutations in COL3A1 produce phenotypes that overlap with vascular EDS. They suggested that the major effect of many dominant mutations in the 'minor' collagen genes may act through protein deficiency rather than through incorporation of structurally altered molecules into fibrils.
quotes: the phenotypes produced by these mutations in COL3A1 overlap with those of the vascular form of EDS.

This suggests that the major effect of many of these dominant mutations in the "minor" collagen genes may be expressed through protein deficiency rather than through incorporation of structurally altered molecules into fibrils.

notes.statement: Liu et al. (1997) inactivated the Col3a1 gene in mouse embryonic stem cells by homologous recombination. About 10% of homozygous mutant mice survived to adulthood, but their life span was much shorter than that of wild-type mice. The major cause of death was rupture of the major blood vessels, similar to patients with type IV Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
quotes: we have inactivated the Col3a1 gene in embryonic stem cells by homologous recombination
About 10% of the homozygous mutant animals survived to adulthood but have a much shorter life span compared with wild-type mice.
The major cause of death of mutant mice was rupture of the major blood vessels, similar to patients with type IV Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.

notes.statement: Liu et al. (1997) found by ultrastructural analysis of tissues from Col3a1-null mice that type III collagen was essential for normal collagen I fibrillogenesis in the cardiovascular system and other organs.
quotes: Ultrastructural analysis of tissues from mutant mice revealed that type III collagen is essential for normal collagen I fibrillogenesis in the cardiovascular system and other organs.
